Fan noise at 2800rpm. Makes a grinding noise at 75% fan speed. AMD drivers have the fan speed set to 100% by default at minimal heat.  I have mine at -35mv and -10 power limit. The card will still boost to 3.1ghz and the Hotspot temp is only 80c. Vram will hit 90c.  I only lost 50mhz and temps went down 5c.  MSI afterburner does not yet fully work with the card right now.  This card compared to my 6800xt in 5120x1440p gets around 40% more frames and the RT performance has also doubled if not more. But RT demanding games still isnt there yet.  Only a 5090 can handle true RT or pathtracing games in 4k.  I paid $729 for my card which is still about 50$ more han what it should of been.  Do not pay $850 for a 9079XT or 5070ti.  That is nearly $200 over priced for a mid-range card.  

This card is a compact card at the cost of vram temps. It does run a lot cooler than my 6800XT I can say.  Noise levels are higher but you want good ventilation on the sides of your case as this card puts out 330 watts of heat.  With my side panel off my case the card drops another 5c.  Really if you had a fan on the side of the case these newer cards will run much cooler. Or an open case.  There is a 28c delta between the hotspot and gpu temp sensors which isn't good. I believe these early cards need to have thermal paste re-applied to the die. But doing so voids the warranty. I really want to do this with my card. All of the heat is coming from the left side of the card mounted in my pc. Also you need a bigger case for airflow with these 300 watt or higher gpus. I have a 4000D case and it's a glass side panel. You need something with a mesh side panel or vents on the side panel for the airflow of these high wattage cards. I have 5 120mm fans and it's not enough for the heat this card puts out. Taking off my side panel drops temps by 7c. Putting the vram temps from 94 max to 87 max. Having vram temps in the 90s is NOT good and the card will not last long

I had no issue with my previous Samsung 980. I bought a Samsung 990 PRO SSD 4 TB on November 18, 2024 from Amazon. I had no trouble transferring my data from my previous NVME. It worked flawlessly in my PC for about 6 months. Then suddenly it would spontaneously reboot my computer and then fail to be detected so my system would just be sitting on the BIOS screen. It would take a hard shut off and turn on to get it to work again. So I foolishly bought another Samsung 990 PRO SSD 4 TB on July 20, 2025 from Amazon. I had no trouble transferring my data from the previous Samsung 990 PRO SSD 4 TB. The problem then disappeared completely with the new 990 PRO.

Now, two months later with again no changes to my system in any way... the problem is back on the new 990 PRO. I wish I would have read reviews of other people having this exact same problem. The Magician app shows it is failing randomly when the NVME is as cool as 38 degrees centigrade.

I have been in professional IT for 30 years and have never experienced something like this. Either these have a design issue that many other people are experiencing based on reviews or I have been incredibly unlucky.

This is the most comfortable and slick feeling keyboard I've had in decades of pc'ing. I mean, it has to "sharp/softness" to it that can't be compared to mechanical keys. This is though my first magnetic so maybe that's why I'm all giddy over it. Regardless, I've had some top tier keyboards. I wanted this one because first, looks. I mean, that's real wood on the side. And the keyboard body is itself - HIGH QUALITY. It's a little weighting but I don't care about that because I'm not walking around with my keyboard. It stays placed and won't budge.


Connection is pretty simple. It can be wired or wireless. I have had it wired but will be doing wireless soon. I've to do some re-arranging and definitely look forward to getting rid of the cable.


Pros: Typing that's feels so good you'd not want to stop typing. The magnetism creating the springing touch is excellent. And I like the fact it can be adjusted. The keyboard is of high quality material. You won't feel ripped off at all if you get this keyboard. And the sound is excellent. Not banging or hard noise clicks. The keyboard layout is standard. Though I'm a gamer and editor I'm from the old school. And I still prefer a keypad. The F keys are also standard with functions tied in to them be default. This keyboard is a looker. And it feels so good to type on. It almost enhances one's WPM.


Cons: I'm maybe spoiled from previous keyboards I've owned. But, I do not like that there is no volume knob. Instead, one has to hold down the "fn" (function) key and then whatever function you want to control (i.e. volume). I mean, a knob is quick and easy. Also, this keyboard has RGB. But, the light is very dull. Even when it's maxed out. I'm not expecting the bat signal, but, compared to other keyboards, this max seems like the minimum on other keyboards. I wish it could be more powerful.


Overall: I'm VERY happy with this keyboard. There were a few sacrifices feature wise, but absolutely no regrets. I highly recommend it.

This is one of the best portable power banks I’ve used. The charging speed is solid, and the wireless function works well without constantly needing to adjust the connection. The magnetic hold is strong and keeps everything aligned while charging.


I also like the digital display. It shows the remaining power clearly, which makes it easy to manage usage. Another plus is that it can charge itself while wirelessly charging your phone, which is convenient when you’re short on outlets.


The only downside is that it doesn’t charge an Apple Watch as fast as it does a phone. It still works, just slower by comparison.


Overall, very reliable, well designed, and easy to use.

I have used Samsung SSD drives for many years exclusively. They have always been the fastest, most reliable SSD drives you could buy. They were more expensive...but worth it.

This one...definitely not. It's very fast. However it has a critical design issue that I wish I had known about before I bought it, which makes it very unreliable.

I purchased this drive for a new PC build. It worked great for three months. After that, at random times, the drive began to vanish. It would disappear as if it had been unplugged. If the PC was using it as its system drive (and it was), the PC would crash and reboot to a BIOS screen. Rebooting the PC does not fix it, the PC has to be physically power cycled for the drive to come back up and reappear.

No data was lost...but it became extremely unreliable, crashing and disappearing more than once a day. I opened a warranty ticket with Samsung, and they replaced it, no questions asked.

Two months later...the replacement drive they provided is now doing the exact same thing. I now have ANOTHER warranty replacement claim open with Samsung.

I did a search online, and there are MANY people complaining about this problem with the Samsung 990 drive. There is obviously something very wrong with the design of the drive, but this problem is known and widespread.

For this reason I recommend you do NOT buy this drive.

wanted to love this card. On paper, the performance looked amazing. Reddit said it was “destroying NVIDIA.” Benchmark videos made it sound like the second coming of PC gaming.

Reality?

I spent more time:

uninstalling drivers
disabling Windows features
tweaking power limits
turning off overlays
reading Reddit threads
praying to the shader cache gods

…than actually playing games.

At one point I had:

driver-only install
HAGS disabled
overlays disabled
clocks lowered
power reduced
three separate PCIe cables connected

And the system still randomly rebooted while sailing around in Windrose like the GPU was allergic to boats.

Meanwhile my old GTX 1080 Ti — a card old enough to qualify for antique plates — just sat there quietly doing its job.

The final straw was swapping in an RTX 5070 OC and instantly getting:

smoother gameplay
higher FPS
lower heat
no weird visual glitches
no random restarts
no emotional damage

The 9070 XT may benchmark well in controlled YouTube environments powered by hope and sponsorships, but in my real-world experience it felt like I had volunteered to become part of AMD’s QA department.

Returned.
